notes.statement: Hayward et al. (2017) analyzed whole-genome sequences from cutaneous, acral, and mucosal melanomas. Cutaneous melanoma was heavily mutated, with novel mutation signatures attributable to ultraviolet radiation. Acral and mucosal melanomas were dominated by structural changes and by mutation signatures of unknown cause. Significantly mutated genes were BRAF, CDKN2A, NRAS, and TP53 in cutaneous melanoma; BRAF, NRAS, and NF1 in acral melanoma; and SF3B1 in mucosal melanoma.
quotes: The heavily mutated landscape of coding and non-coding mutations in cutaneous melanoma resolved novel signatures of mutagenesis attributable to ultraviolet radiation. However, acral and mucosal melanomas were dominated by structural changes and mutation signatures of unknown aetiology, not previously identified in melanoma.
Significantly mutated genes included BRAF, CDKN2A, NRAS and TP53 in cutaneous melanoma, BRAF, NRAS and NF1 in acral melanoma and SF3B1 in mucosal melanoma.

notes.statement: Hayward et al. (2017) found that TERT promoter mutations were the most frequent mutations in melanoma. However, neither these nor ATRX mutations were associated with greater telomere length. About as many genes were affected by recurrent noncoding mutations as by recurrent coding mutations. Most melanomas had potentially actionable mutations, mostly in the MAPK and phosphoinositol kinase pathways.
quotes: Mutations affecting the TERT promoter were the most frequent of all; however, neither they nor ATRX mutations, which correlate with alternative telomere lengthening, were associated with greater telomere length.
The number of genes affected by recurrent mutations disrupting non-coding sequences was similar to that affected by recurrent mutations to coding sequences.
Most melanomas had potentially actionable mutations, most in components of the mitogen-activated protein kinase and phosphoinositol kinase pathways.

notes.statement: Van Allen et al. (2015) performed whole-exome sequencing on pretreatment tumor and matched germline samples from 110 patients with metastatic melanoma treated with the anti-CTLA-4 antibody ipilimumab. Patients who got clinical benefit had a significantly higher nonsynonymous mutational load (P = 0.0076) and neoantigen load (P = 0.027). No gene, including BRAF and NRAS, was enriched for mutations in either response group.
quotes: we analyzed whole exomes from pretreatment melanoma tumor biopsies and matching germline tissue samples from 110 patients
Overall, nonsynonymous mutational load was significantly associated with clinical benefit from ipilimumab (P = 0.0076; Mann-Whitney test)
No genes were enriched for nonsynonymous mutations, including BRAF and NRAS, in the patient subgroups that had clinical benefit or no clinical benefit

notes.statement: Van Allen et al. (2015) found no recurrent neoantigen peptide sequences that predicted response to ipilimumab, and a previously reported tetrapeptide signature was not enriched in responders. In tumor transcriptome data, expression of the cytolytic markers GZMA and PRF1, and of CTLA4 and PD-L2, was significantly higher in patients with clinical benefit. This suggested that expression of immune checkpoint molecules may correlate with response to immunotherapy.
quotes: However, no recurrent neoantigen peptide sequences predicted responder patient populations.

Expression of CTLA-4 itself and of the programmed cell death 1 ligand 2 (PD-L2), which inhibits peripheral T cell proteins, was also significantly elevated in the cohort that showed clinical benefit compared with the one that showed no clinical benefit (P = 0.033 and P = 0.041; Mann-Whitney)
Both genes were significantly enriched in the cohort treated with ipilimumab that had clinical benefit compared with the cohort that showed no clinical benefit (P = 0.042; Mann-Whitney)

notes.statement: Snyder et al. (2014) performed whole-exome sequencing of melanoma tumors and matched blood from 64 patients treated with the anti-CTLA-4 antibodies ipilimumab or tremelimumab. In both a discovery set of 25 patients and a validation set of 39 patients, mutational load was significantly associated with long-term clinical benefit. However, a high mutational load alone was not sufficient to predict benefit.
quotes: Malignant melanoma exomes from 64 patients treated with CTLA-4 blockade were characterized with the use of massively parallel sequencing.

There was a significant difference in mutational load between patients with a long-term clinical benefit and those with a minimal benefit or no benefit, both in the discovery set (P = 0.01 by the Mann–Whitney test) and in the validation set (P = 0.009 by the Mann–Whitney test)

notes.statement: Snyder et al. (2014) found 101 candidate tetrapeptide neoepitopes that were shared only among discovery-set patients with a long-term benefit from CTLA-4 blockade. This neoepitope signature correlated strongly with overall survival in both the discovery and validation sets. Some of these neoepitopes were homologous to viral and bacterial antigens.
quotes: included 101 shared exclusively among patients in the discovery set who had a long-term clinical benefit; this was also independently observed in the validation set
The neoepitope signature derived from the discovery set correlated strongly with survival in both the discovery and validation sets (P<0.001 for both comparisons by the log-rank test)

notes.statement: Snyder et al. (2014) showed that predicted neoantigens activated patients' T cells. A mutant peptide arising from a somatic FAM3C mutation (p.K193E) caused a polyfunctional T-cell response in one patient. Another mutant peptide, from a CSMD1 mutation (p.G3446E), caused a similar response in a second patient. The corresponding nonmutant peptides did not.
quotes: We found a polyfunctional T-cell response to the peptide TESPFEQHI in Patient CR9306 (Fig. S10D in the Supplementary Appendix) but not to its nonmutant counterpart, TKSPFEQHI.
TESPFEQHI results from a mutation in FAM3C (c.A577G;p.K193E), a gene highly expressed in melanoma
GLEREGFTF arises from a mutation in CSMD1 (c.G10337A;p.G3446E), which is also highly expressed in melanoma

notes.statement: Sun et al. (2014) found that 6 of 16 melanoma tumors analyzed acquired EGFR expression after developing resistance to BRAF or MEK inhibitors. They found evidence of SOX10 loss and/or activated TGF-beta signaling in 4 of the 6 EGFR-positive drug-resistant patient samples.
quotes: Here we show that 6 out of 16 melanoma tumours analysed acquired EGFR expression after the development of resistance to BRAF or MEK inhibitors.
We find evidence for SOX10 loss and/or activation of TGF-β signalling in 4 of the 6 EGFR-positive drug-resistant melanoma patient samples.

notes.statement: Using an shRNA library focused on chromatin regulators, Sun et al. (2014) found that suppressing SOX10 in melanoma cells activated TGF-beta signaling. This led to upregulation of EGFR and PDGFRB, which conferred resistance to BRAF and MEK inhibitors. EGFR expression or TGF-beta treatment caused slow growth with hallmarks of oncogene-induced senescence, but became beneficial for proliferation when BRAF or MEK inhibitors were present.
quotes: we find that suppression of sex determining region Y-box 10 (SOX10) in melanoma causes activation of TGF-β signalling, thus leading to upregulation of EGFR and platelet-derived growth factor receptor-β (PDGFRB), which confer resistance to BRAF and MEK inhibitors.

Expression of EGFR in melanoma or treatment with TGF-β results in a slow-growth phenotype with cells displaying hallmarks of oncogene-induced senescence. However, EGFR expression or exposure to TGF-β becomes beneficial for proliferation in the presence of BRAF or MEK inhibitors.

notes.statement: Sun et al. (2014) found that in mixed melanoma cell populations, cells with low SOX10 and high EGFR were rapidly enriched during drug treatment, but this enrichment reversed when treatment stopped. They suggested this explains why some patients with BRAF- or MEK-inhibitor-resistant melanoma may regain drug sensitivity after a 'drug holiday'. They identified patients with EGFR-positive melanoma as a group that may benefit from re-treatment.
quotes: cells with low SOX10 and consequently high EGFR expression are rapidly enriched in the presence of drug, but this is reversed when the drug treatment is discontinued.

Our findings provide a rationale for why some BRAF or MEK inhibitor-resistant melanoma patients may regain sensitivity to these drugs after a 'drug holiday' and identify patients with EGFR-positive melanoma as a group that may benefit from re-treatment after a drug holiday.

notes.statement: Huang et al. (2013) found 2 mutually exclusive somatic C>T mutations (C228T and C250T) in the TERT core promoter in 50 of 70 (71%) melanomas. Both mutations lay within 100 bp of the transcription start site and carried a UV-damage signature. In whole-genome sequencing data, these promoter mutations were among the 4 most recurrent melanoma nucleotide substitutions, alongside BRAF V600E and NRAS Q61R.
quotes: Together, these TERT promoter mutations were observed in 50 of 70 (71%; 95% confidence interval: 59 to 82%, Clopper-Pearson method) melanomas examined (Fig. 1B and table S1).
Moreover, the mutations were mutually exclusive in both the discovery and extension sets (P = 5.4 × 10−7, Fisher’s one-sided exact test).

notes.statement: Huang et al. (2013) found that both the C228T and C250T TERT promoter mutations created a consensus binding motif for ETS transcription factors. In luciferase reporter assays in 5 cell lines, each mutation increased transcriptional activity from the TERT promoter about 2- to 4-fold compared with the wildtype promoter.
quotes: Both C228T and C250T generated an identical 11-bp nucleotide stretch (5′-CCCCTTCCGGG-3′) containing a consensus binding site for E-twenty-six (ETS) transcription factors (GGAA, reverse complement) within the TERT promoter region.
In comparison to the wild-type TERT promoter, both mutations conferred approximately two- to fourfold increased transcriptional activity in five distinct cell line contexts (Fig. 1C and fig. S1D).

notes.statement: Huang et al. (2013) found C228T or C250T in 24 of 150 (16%) cancer cell lines. The mutations were seen in 5 of 6 melanoma lines, and there was preliminary evidence of a higher frequency in bladder (3 of 3) and hepatocellular (4 of 6) cancer cell lines.
quotes: Overall, 24 CCLE lines (16%) contained either C228T or C250T (mean allelic fraction, 0.61; range, 0.17 to 1.00) (table S1).

An increased frequency in melanoma was again noted (five of six lines tested), with additional evidence suggesting possible heightened prevalence (>25%; one-sided 95% confidence interval) in bladder (three of three lines) and hepatocellular cancer cell lines (four of six lines) (Fig. 1D).

notes.statement: Horn et al. (2013) found that the germline TERT promoter mutation created a new binding motif for Ets transcription factors and ternary complex factors (TCFs) near the transcription start. In reporter gene assays, it caused up to a twofold increase in transcription.
quotes: The mutation creates a new binding motif for Ets transcription factors and ternary complex factors (TCFs) near the transcription start and, in reporter gene assays, caused up to twofold increase in transcription.

notes.statement: In sporadic melanoma, Horn et al. (2013) found recurrent somatic TERT promoter mutations with an ultraviolet signature. These occurred in 125 of 168 (74%) cell lines derived from metastatic melanomas, in 45 of 53 (85%) corresponding metastatic tumor tissues, and in 25 of 77 (33%) primary melanomas. Most of the mutations were at two positions and generated binding motifs for Ets/TCF transcription factors.
quotes: observed recurrent ultraviolet signature somatic mutations in 125 of 168 (74%) of human cell lines derived from metastatic melanomas, 45 of 53 corresponding metastatic tumor tissues (85%), and 25 of 77 (33%) primary melanomas
The majority of those mutations occurred at two positions in the TERT promoter and also generated binding motifs for Ets/TCF transcription factors.

notes.statement: Das Thakur et al. (2013) modeled vemurafenib resistance in a patient-derived BRAF(V600E) melanoma xenograft (HMEX1906) treated continuously with vemurafenib. Resistant tumors still depended on BRAF(V600E)-MEK-ERK signaling because they expressed more BRAF(V600E). One resistant tumor had BRAF amplification (about 14 copies vs about 6). Exome sequencing found no secondary mutations in BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, HRAS, or MEK1.
quotes: In one of these models, resistant tumours show continued dependency on BRAF(V600E)→MEK→ERK signalling owing to elevated BRAF(V600E) expression.
the 45V-RT5 tumour was found to have ~14 copies of BRAFT1799A (Fig. 2c), consistent with BRAF amplification as a mechanism of vemurafenib resistance
exome sequence analysis failed to reveal secondary mutations in the coding sequences of BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, HRAS or MEK1 in resistant tumours

notes.statement: Das Thakur et al. (2013) found that vemurafenib-resistant melanoma cells became dependent on the drug to proliferate. Cultured resistant cells grew best at 50 nM vemurafenib. Stopping the drug raised ERK signaling and caused established resistant tumors to regress, suggesting that too much BRAF(V600E) signaling creates a fitness deficit when the drug is absent.
quotes: Most importantly, we demonstrate that vemurafenib-resistant melanomas become drug dependent for their continued proliferation, such that cessation of drug administration leads to regression of established drug-resistant tumours.
a cell-proliferation assay conducted with a range of drug concentrations indicated a bell-shaped response to vemurafenib, with peak proliferation in the resistant cells occurring at 50 nM vemurafenib
drug withdrawal led to elevated pMEK1/2→pERK1/2 signalling, concomitant with tumour regression

notes.statement: Das Thakur et al. (2013) found that intermittent vemurafenib dosing (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off) prevented lethal drug-resistant disease in xenograft models. Mice dosed continuously developed lethal resistant disease within 100 days, whereas none of the intermittently dosed mice did over 200 days. A second patient-derived xenograft (HMEX2613) gave similar results.
quotes: mice continuously dosed with vemurafenib developed lethal drug-resistant disease within 100 days after initiation of drug administration. By contrast, none of the mice on the intermittent dosing schedule developed drug-resistant disease over the course of 200 days
these results indicate that intermittent dosing significantly delays the onset of drug resistance by exploiting the fitness deficit shown by drug-resistant tumour cells in the absence of drug

notes.statement: Wilson et al. (2012) found that hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) reduced sensitivity to the BRAF inhibitor PLX4032 (vemurafenib) in BRAF-mutant melanoma cell lines. MET expression correlated with HGF rescue, and the MET inhibitor crizotinib blocked the rescue. Of 446 secreted factors screened, HGF was one of very few that could rescue BRAF-mutant melanoma cells from PLX4032.
quotes: Notably, among 446 tested secreted factors, HGF was among a very small number that could rescue BRAF-mutant melanoma cells from PLX4032 sensitivity (Supplementary Fig. 8).
Among 12 additional BRAF-mutant melanoma cell lines tested, HGF significantly attenuated PLX4032 sensitivity in 5 lines (Fig. 4a).
As anticipated, rescue by HGF was blocked when MET was inhibited by crizotinib (Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 9a).

notes.statement: In xenografts of BRAF-mutant 928MEL and 624MEL melanoma cells, Wilson et al. (2012) found that activating MET with an agonistic antibody strongly reduced the growth-suppressive effect of PLX4032. Inhibiting MET increased tumor regression with PLX4032.
quotes: Activation of MET in tumours using the MET-agonistic antibody 3D6 strongly abrogated the growth-suppressive effects of PLX4032 (Fig. 4c).
Inhibiting MET enhanced the effect of PLX4032 on tumour regression (Fig. 4c), with more partial responses observed in the 928MEL model (Supplementary Fig. 10).

notes.statement: Wilson et al. (2012) measured pretreatment plasma HGF in 126 patients with BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma treated with PLX4032 in the BRIM2 trial. Higher plasma HGF was associated with worse progression-free survival (hazard ratio, 1.42) and overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.8). Because the trial had a single arm, the authors could not determine whether HGF confers drug resistance.
quotes: Pre-treatment plasma HGF levels were measured from 126 of the 132 patients enrolled onto the BRIM2 clinical trial (BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma patients treated with PLX4032).
Increased plasma HGF was associated with worse outcome as measured by progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio, 1.42; P <0.005) and overall survival (OS; hazard ratio, 1.8; P <0.001; Fig. 4d, e).
it is not possible to determine whether higher HGF levels confer drug resistance

notes.statement: Straussman et al. (2012) found that HGF secreted by stromal fibroblasts activated the MET receptor. This reactivated both the MAPK and the PI3K-AKT pathways and gave BRAF V600E melanoma cell lines immediate, innate resistance to the RAF inhibitor PLX4720. Blocking HGF or MET (with crizotinib) reversed the resistance, which the authors suggested supports combining RAF and HGF or MET inhibitors as treatment.
quotes: Proteomic analysis showed that stromal cell secretion of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) resulted in activation of the HGF receptor MET, reactivation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase (PI(3)K)-AKT signalling pathways, and immediate resistance to RAF inhibition.

Dual inhibition of RAF and either HGF or MET resulted in reversal of drug resistance, suggesting RAF plus HGF or MET inhibitory combination therapy as a potential therapeutic strategy for BRAF-mutant melanoma.

notes.statement: Straussman et al. (2012) detected HGF in tumour-associated stromal cells in 23 of 34 pre-treatment biopsies from patients with BRAF V600E melanoma. Patients with stromal HGF had a significantly poorer response to BRAF inhibitor treatment than those without it.
quotes: HGF was detected in the tumor-associated stromal cells in 23/34 patients (68%)
Indeed, patients with stromal HGF had a significantly poorer response to treatment compared to those lacking expression (P < 0.05; Fig 3c).

notes.statement: Nikolaev et al. (2011) performed exome sequencing of 7 melanoma cell lines and donor-matched germline cells. All melanoma samples had high numbers of somatic mutations showing the hallmark of UV-induced DNA repair. This hallmark was absent in tumor sample-specific mutations in 2 metastases derived from the same individual.
quotes: We performed exome sequencing to detect somatic mutations in protein-coding regions in seven melanoma cell lines and donor-matched germline cells.
All melanoma samples had high numbers of somatic mutations, which showed the hallmark of UV-induced DNA repair.

notes.statement: Nikolaev et al. (2011) found gain-of-function MAP2K1 (MEK1) and MAP2K2 (MEK2) mutations in 2 melanomas with noncanonical BRAF mutations. These mutations resulted in constitutive ERK phosphorylation and higher resistance to MEK inhibitors. Screening a larger cohort of individuals with melanoma revealed recurrent somatic MAP2K1 and MAP2K2 mutations at an overall frequency of 8%.
quotes: Two melanomas with non-canonical BRAF mutations harbored gain-of-function MAP2K1 and MAP2K2 (MEK1 and MEK2, respectively) mutations, resulting in constitutive ERK phosphorylation and higher resistance to MEK inhibitors.
Screening a larger cohort of individuals with melanoma revealed the presence of recurring somatic MAP2K1 and MAP2K2 mutations, which occurred at an overall frequency of 8%.

notes.statement: Nikolaev et al. (2011) frequently found somatic missense and nonsense mutations in 3 candidate melanoma genes: FAT4, LRP1B, and DSC1.
quotes: Furthermore, missense and nonsense somatic mutations were frequently found in three candidate melanoma genes, FAT4, LRP1B and DSC1.

notes.statement: Stark et al. (2011) sequenced the exomes of 8 metastatic melanoma cell lines and their matched lymphoblastoid lines. They found 3,215 somatic alterations, and the mutation spectrum matched the signature of ultraviolet light exposure. A prevalence screen then found somatic nonsynonymous mutations in MAP3K5 in 8 of 85 melanoma cell lines and in MAP3K9 in 13 of 85, so 24% of samples carried a mutation in one of the two genes.
quotes: Overall, 3,215 somatic alterations were identified; range 243-523 per sample (Supplementary Table 2).
A prevalence screen revealed 8/85 melanoma cell lines with somatic non-synonymous mutations in MAP3K5 (8 mutations) and 13/85 cell lines with mutations in MAP3K9 (total of 18 mutations) (Fig. 1).
Overall, MAP3K5 and MAP3K9 were mutated in 9% and 15% of melanoma cell lines respectively and mutation of either gene occurred in 24% of samples.

notes.statement: Stark et al. (2011) found that, with one exception, MAP3K5 and MAP3K9 mutations did not occur together in the same cell line, suggesting that both target the same pathway. They found loss of heterozygosity at MAP3K5 in 85% of melanoma samples and at MAP3K9 in 67%. The mutations did not correlate with mutations or deletions of BRAF, NRAS, CDKN2A, PTEN, or TP53.
quotes: With the exception of one cell line, mutations in MAP3K5 or MAP3K9 were mutually exclusive (Supplementary Table 6), suggesting they may target the same pathway.
showed that 98/115 (85%) and 77/115 (67%) samples had LOH for MAP3K5 or MAP3K9 respectively (Supplementary Fig 3).
Mutations in MAP3K5 and MAP3K9 were not correlated with mutations/deletions of BRAF, NRAS, CDKN2A, PTEN, or TP53 (Supplementary Table 6).

notes.statement: In in vitro kinase assays, Stark et al. (2011) found that the MAP3K9 W333X mutant reduced kinase activity against myelin basic protein by 95% and the MAP3K5 I780F mutant reduced it by 93%. In HEK293T cells, expressing the mutants reduced downstream JNK and MEK/ERK signaling. Knocking down MAP3K9 with siRNA increased the viability of melanoma cells after temozolomide treatment, suggesting that reduced MAP3K9 activity can contribute to chemoresistance.
quotes: MAP3K9 K171A and W333X mutants showed a 92% and 95% reduction in kinase activity against MBP relative to the wild type enzyme (p<0.001). Additionally, MAP3K5 I780F almost completely abolishes kinase activity (93% reduction relative to wild type, p<0.01)
Expression of either mutant MAP3K9 protein (W333X and control K171A) resulted in decreased signaling through MAP2K4/7-JNK and MEK1/2-ERK (Fig. 4b)
This suggests that attenuated MAP3K9 activity can contribute to chemotherapeutic resistance in melanoma.

notes.statement: In a phase 3 randomized trial of 675 patients with previously untreated metastatic melanoma carrying the BRAF V600E mutation, Chapman et al. (2011) found that vemurafenib, compared with dacarbazine, was associated with a relative reduction of 63% in the risk of death and 74% in the risk of death or disease progression. At 6 months, overall survival was 84% with vemurafenib and 64% with dacarbazine.
quotes: We conducted a phase 3 randomized clinical trial comparing vemurafenib with dacarbazine in 675 patients with previously untreated, metastatic melanoma with the BRAF V600E mutation.
At 6 months, overall survival was 84% (95% confidence interval [CI], 78 to 89) in the vemurafenib group and 64% (95% CI, 56 to 73) in the dacarbazine group.

vemurafenib was associated with a relative reduction of 63% in the risk of death and of 74% in the risk of either death or disease progression, as compared with dacarbazine (P<0.001 for both comparisons)

notes.statement: Chapman et al. (2011) reported confirmed response rates of 48% with vemurafenib and 5% with dacarbazine. Median progression-free survival was 5.3 months with vemurafenib versus 1.6 months with dacarbazine. Four of 10 patients with BRAF V600K mutations responded to vemurafenib, which suggested that melanomas with this variant are also sensitive to the drug.
quotes: Response rates were 48% for vemurafenib and 5% for dacarbazine.
The estimated median progression-free survival was 5.3 months in the vemurafenib group and 1.6 months in the dacarbazine group.
Furthermore, 4 of 10 patients with the BRAF V600K mutation had a response to vemurafenib, indicating that melanomas with this variant are also sensitive to vemurafenib.

notes.statement: Chapman et al. (2011) found that 18% of vemurafenib-treated patients developed cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma, or both, all of which were treated by simple excision. The authors speculated that these lesions arise because vemurafenib paradoxically activates the MAPK pathway in cells with wild-type BRAF. Other common adverse events included arthralgia, rash, fatigue, and photosensitivity, and 38% of patients required dose modification.
quotes: In the vemurafenib group, a cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma, or both developed in 61 patients (18%). All lesions were treated by simple excision.
it is speculated to involve the activating effect of vemurafenib on preneoplastic cells in which wild-type BRAF is further primed by upstream pathway activation.

Common adverse events associated with vemurafenib were arthralgia, rash, fatigue, alopecia, keratoacanthoma or squamous-cell carcinoma, photosensitivity, nausea, and diarrhea; 38% of patients required dose modification because of toxic effects.

notes.statement: Wei et al. (2011) performed whole-exome sequencing of 14 matched normal and metastatic melanoma DNAs and identified 68 genes that appeared to be somatically mutated at elevated frequency. A recurrent somatic TRRAP mutation (p.Ser722Phe) was found in 6 of 167 melanomas (about 4%), and GRIN2A was mutated in 33% of melanoma samples.
quotes: we performed whole-exome sequencing of 14 matched normal and metastatic tumor DNAs. Using stringent criteria, we identified 68 genes that appeared to be somatically mutated at elevated frequency

TRRAP harbored a recurrent mutation that clustered in one position (p. Ser722Phe) in 6 out of 167 affected individuals (∼4%), as well as a previously unidentified gene, GRIN2A, which was mutated in 33% of melanoma samples.

notes.statement: Wei et al. (2011) found a predominance of C>T/G>A transitions and CC>TT/GG>AA dinucleotide substitutions among melanoma somatic mutations, consistent with an ultraviolet light exposure signature.
quotes: Finally, we observed a total of 116 dinucleotide substitutions; of these, 59 were CC>TT/GG>AA changes, all consistent with the previously documented ultraviolet light exposure signature.

notes.statement: Wei et al. (2011) found that mutant TRRAP (p.Ser722Phe) transformed NIH 3T3 cells more efficiently than wildtype TRRAP, and that shRNA knockdown of TRRAP increased apoptosis in melanoma lines carrying mutant TRRAP but had minimal effect in wildtype lines, suggesting that TRRAP functions as an oncogene.
quotes: Two weeks after transfection, mutant TRRAP transformed NIH 3T3 cells more efficiently than wild-type TRRAP (Fig. 2a).

Knockdown of TRRAP had minimal effect on the survival of cells expressing wild-type TRRAP but substantially increased apoptosis rates of melanoma lines carrying mutant TRRAP, particularly when the clones were grown in low serum

notes.statement: Wei et al. (2011) found by pathway analysis that the glutamate signaling pathway was highly significantly mutated in melanoma, with GRIN2A, encoding an NMDA receptor subunit, being the most highly mutated gene and PLCB4 also frequently mutated. The mechanism by which GRIN2A mutations act was unclear.
quotes: From this analysis, we found the glutamate signaling pathway to be highly significant.

Based on this classification, the mechanism by which mutations in GRIN2A have a tumorigenic effect is unclear; however, their frequency strongly suggests that they play a major role in melanoma and are worthy of future investigation.

notes.statement: Gaffal et al. (2011) gave 15 newborn Hgf-Cdk4(R24C) mice on the pigmented C57BL/6 background a single erythemogenic dose of UVB (6 kJ/m2) and compared them with 30 untreated Hgf-Cdk4(R24C) mice. Neonatal UVB exposure shortened the latency and sped up the growth of primary melanomas. It also shortened the time from melanoma onset to melanoma-related death (61 vs 96 days), but it did not change the development of melanocytic nevi.
quotes: Neonatal UVB exposure decreased the latency and accelerated the growth of primary melanomas resulting in a significantly decreased time from melanoma onset to melanoma-related death (61 days vs. 96 days). Interestingly, we did not observe differences in the development of melanocytic nevi.

notes.statement: Gaffal et al. (2011) found that UVB-induced melanomas in Hgf-Cdk4(R24C) mice were more aggressive, with more tumor cell proliferation, invasive growth, and angiogenesis. Lung metastases were more frequent in irradiated mice than in untreated mice (73% vs 47%). The UVB-induced tumors contained very few infiltrating immune cells and expressed very low levels of proinflammatory chemokines. The authors suggested that the molecular targets of UVB help transformed melanocytes bypass proliferative arrest without triggering a cellular immune response.
quotes: UVB irradiation shifted the spectrum of melanomas toward a more aggressive phenotype with increased tumor cell proliferation, invasive growth and enhanced angiogenesis
we observed distal melanoma metastases in the lungs more frequently in the UV-irradiated than in the untreated cohort of Hgf-Cdk4(R24C) mice (73% vs. 47%)
supports the hypothesis that the molecular targets of UVB are involved in bypassing the proliferative arrest of transformed melanocytes without alerting a cellular immune response

notes.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) described the structure-guided discovery of PLX4032 (RG7204), a selective inhibitor of oncogenic B-RAF(V600E) kinase activity that blocked the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway in BRAF-mutant cells and caused regression of BRAF-mutant xenografts, with no effect on xenografts in which both BRAF alleles were wildtype.
quotes: Preclinical experiments demonstrated that PLX4032 selectively blocked the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway in BRAF mutant cells and caused regression of BRAF mutant xenografts.
By contrast, no effect was observed on melanoma xenograft growth if both BRAF alleles were wild-type.

notes.statement: In a phase 1 trial, Bollag et al. (2010) found that 24 of 32 patients with BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma treated with PLX4032 at the maximum tolerated dose of 960 mg twice daily had partial responses and 2 had complete responses (81% response rate); no patient whose melanoma lacked a BRAF mutation responded. Two responders carried BRAF V600K rather than V600E.
quotes: Out of the 32 patients treated at this dose, 24 experienced tumor regressions qualifying as PRs and two patients had CRs.
none of the patients with melanomas lacking BRAF mutations achieved PR
tumors from the two patients lacking the BRAFV600E mutation were found to carry the BRAFV600K mutation and were among the better responders (71% and 100% reduction in tumor dimensions)

notes.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) found in paired tumor biopsies that clinical response to PLX4032 required greater than 80% inhibition of cytoplasmic ERK phosphorylation, indicating that near-complete inhibition of ERK signaling may be needed for significant tumor response; reductions in FDG uptake on PET were seen after 2 weeks of treatment.
quotes: In patients with tumor regressions, pathway analysis typically showed greater than 80% inhibition of cytoplasmic ERK phosphorylation (Figure 3C). This result indicates that near-complete inhibition of ERK signaling may be needed for significant tumor response.
All of the assessable patients treated with MBP-formulated PLX4032 experienced major reductions in FDG uptake.

notes.statement: Bollag et al. (2010) reported that 31% of patients treated at the maximum tolerated dose of PLX4032 developed cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas of keratoacanthoma type, possibly related to paradoxical activation of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway via RAF dimerization in wildtype BRAF cells.
quotes: Thirty-one percent of the patients treated at the MTD developed skin lesions described as cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, keratoacanthoma type.

Recent publications suggest a potential mechanism that may in part account for the keratinocyte proliferation noted in the patients on study. These reports follow-up on prior descriptions of paradoxical activation of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway by RAF kinase inhibitors.

notes.statement: In a phase 1 dose-escalation trial of PLX4032 (RG7204), an oral inhibitor of mutant BRAF, Flaherty et al. (2010) set the recommended phase 2 dose at 960 mg twice daily; rash, fatigue, and arthralgia limited further dose increases. Among 16 patients in the dose-escalation cohort who had V600E-mutant melanoma and received 240 mg or more twice daily, 10 had a partial response and 1 had a complete response. In the extension cohort of 32 patients, 24 had a partial response and 2 had a complete response.
quotes: The recommended phase 2 dose was 960 mg twice daily, with increases in the dose limited by grade 2 or 3 rash, fatigue, and arthralgia.
Among the 32 patients in the extension cohort, 24 had a partial response and 2 had a complete response. The estimated median progression-free survival among all patients was more than 7 months.

notes.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) found that none of 5 patients whose metastatic melanoma lacked a BRAF mutation showed tumor regression on PLX4032. In V600E-mutant melanoma, responses lasted from 2 to more than 18 months, and some tumors became resistant. The authors had not seen 'gatekeeper' BRAF mutations in resistant tumors.
quotes: A total of 5 patients with metastatic melanoma whose tumors did not have a BRAF mutation received doses of 240 mg or more twice daily. None had evidence of tumor regression during the study
To date, we have not seen “gatekeeper” BRAF mutations in resistant tumors, although this issue requires more investigation.

notes.statement: Flaherty et al. (2010) reported cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas, nearly all of keratoacanthoma type, in 8 patients (15%) in the dose-escalation cohort and 10 patients (31%) in the extension cohort treated with PLX4032. The median time to their appearance was 8 weeks. The authors suggested that BRAF inhibitors activating the MAP kinase pathway in cells without a BRAF mutation may account for some side effects.
quotes: Eight patients in the dose-escalation cohort (15%) and 10 patients in the extension cohort (31%) had cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas, with a total of 35 carcinomas.
Recent data show that BRAF inhibitors can activate the MAP kinase pathway in cells that lack a BRAF mutation. This activation may pertain to some of the side effects seen with PLX4032.

notes.statement: In paired tumor biopsies from 7 treated patients, Flaherty et al. (2010) found that phosphorylated ERK, cyclin D1, and Ki-67 were markedly reduced at day 15 of PLX4032 treatment. This suggested that the drug inhibited the MAP kinase pathway in tumors.
quotes: Tumor levels of phosphorylated ERK, cyclin D1, and Ki-67 were markedly reduced at day 15 as compared with baseline in all specimens tested (Fig. 2A). This finding suggests that PLX4032 inhibited the MAP kinase pathway

notes.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) sequenced the genome of a malignant melanoma cell line (COLO-829) and a lymphoblastoid line from the same patient. They identified 33,345 somatic base substitutions, 292 of them in protein-coding sequences, along with small indels and 51 predicted somatic rearrangements.
quotes: We identified 33,345 somatic base substitutions.
A total of 292 somatic base substitutions were in protein-coding sequences (Table 1 and Supplementary Table 4).

notes.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) found that most somatic substitutions in the melanoma genome were C>T/G>A transitions, with 92% at the 3-prime base of pyrimidine dinucleotides. This indicated that most were caused by ultraviolet light-induced DNA damage. Fewer mutations were found on transcribed strands and in highly expressed genes, consistent with transcription-coupled repair.
quotes: A total of 92% of C>T mutations occurred at the 3′ base of a pyrimidine dinucleotide compared with 53% expected by chance (P<0.0001).
Therefore, the mutation spectrum and sequence context indicate that most C>T/G>A somatic substitutions in COLO-829 are attributable to ultraviolet-light-induced DNA damage.
There were 2,773 C>T changes on the transcribed strands and 4,058 on the non-transcribed strands (P<0.0001)

notes.statement: Pleasance et al. (2010) identified 2 somatic missense mutations in SPDEF in COLO-829. Sequencing of 48 additional metastatic melanomas found a further somatic SPDEF mutation (W158X). They also reported missense mutations in MMP28 and UVRAG as candidate cancer gene mutations.
quotes: two heterozygous missense mutations (het, p.S229L; het, p.D283H) were in SPDEF, which encodes a member of the ETS transcription factor family.
Sequencing SPDEF through 48 additional, untreated metastatic melanomas revealed a further somatic mutation (p.W158*).

notes.statement: In a genome-wide association study of nevus count in 1,524 UK female twins, Falchi et al. (2009) replicated the findings in 4,107 Australian adolescent subjects. They found strongly associated variants in MTAP, next to CDKN2A on 9p21 (rs4636294, combined P = 3.4 x 10(-15)), and in PLA2G6 on 22q13.1 (rs2284063, combined P = 3.4 x 10(-8)).
quotes: We identified strongly associated variants in MTAP, a gene adjacent to the familial melanoma susceptibility locus CDKN2A on 9p21 (rs4636294, combined P = 3.4 x 10(-15)), as well as in PLA2G6 on 22q13.1 (rs2284063, combined P = 3.4 x 10(-8)).

notes.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) found that variants at both loci were associated with melanoma risk in 3,131 melanoma cases from two independent studies (Q-MEGA and Leeds). The highest combined odds ratios were 1.23 for rs10757257 at 9p21 (combined P = 3.4 x 10(-8)) and 1.23 for rs132985 at 22q13.1 (combined P = 2.6 x 10(-7)). In the Leeds sample, subjects homozygous for the risk alleles at both loci had double the risk (OR = 1.94).
quotes: variants in these two loci showed association with melanoma risk in 3,131 melanoma cases from two independent studies, including rs10757257 at 9p21, combined P = 3.4 x 10(-8), OR = 1.23 (95% CI = 1.15-1.30) and rs132985 at 22q13.1, combined P = 2.6 x 10(-7), OR = 1.23 (95% CI = 1.15-1.30).
Subjects homozygous at the two loci have double the risk (OR = 1.94; 95% CI = 1.19 – 3.16).

notes.statement: When Falchi et al. (2009) adjusted the association between melanoma and these SNPs for nevus count, the odds ratio moved toward 1.0 and the P value became less significant. They interpreted this as consistent with melanoma risk at these loci being mediated through nevus count.
quotes: When the association between melanoma and SNP was adjusted for nevus count, the OR for melanoma risk was reduced toward 1.0 and the P value became less significant, consistent with melanoma risk being mediated via nevus count.

notes.statement: Falchi et al. (2009) found that UK twins homozygous for the risk variants at both rs4636294 and rs2284063 had more than double the number of nevi of those homozygous for the protective alleles (median 30 vs 12.5). The 9p21 and 22q13 loci each explained a small fraction of the variance in nevus count.
quotes: subjects in the TwinsUK discovery sample homozygous for both variants (7%) had more than double the number of nevi (median number of nevi = 30) compared to subjects homozygous for the protective alleles (median number of nevi = 12.5).
The 9p21 and 22q13 loci accounted for 1.5% (UK) and 3.0% (Australia), and for 1.9% (UK) and 0.7% (Australia) of nevus count variance, respectively.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide association study by the GenoMEL consortium, Bishop et al. (2009) genotyped 317K tagging SNPs in 1,650 selected melanoma cases and 4,336 controls of European ancestry. They replicated the findings in 1,149 cases and 964 controls from GenoMEL and in a population-based Leeds study of 1,163 cases and 903 controls. Three loci were replicated: 16q24 encompassing MC1R, 11q14-q21 encompassing TYR, and 9p21 adjacent to MTAP and flanking CDKN2A.
quotes: We report a genome-wide association study of melanoma conducted by the GenoMEL consortium based on 317K tagging SNPs for 1,650 selected cases and 4,336 controls

Three of these loci were replicated: 16q24 encompassing MC1R (combined P = 2.54 x 10(-27) for rs258322), 11q14-q21 encompassing TYR (P = 2.41 x 10(-14) for rs1393350) and 9p21 adjacent to MTAP and flanking CDKN2A (P = 4.03 x 10(-7) for rs7023329).

notes.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) found that the strongest association was with rs258322 on 16q24 (per-allele OR 1.67). Stepwise regression found an additional SNP, rs8059973, that appeared to be associated with melanoma risk independently of the other 16q24 SNPs. The authors noted that this region also contains CDK10 and FANCA.
quotes: The magnitude of the association with rs258322 (per-allele odds ratio (OR) of 1.67, 95% confidence interval (CI) (1.52, 1.83), Table 1) is notable, since it is comparable to that found by a recent meta-analysis of MC1R variants even though this SNP is distant from MC1R.
one of these (rs8059973) was not reported by the Han et al study and appears to have an association independent of the other two on melanoma risk

notes.statement: At 9p21, Bishop et al. (2009) found association with rs7023329, which lies within the MTAP gene (overall P = 4.03 x 10(-7)). They also found an independent association with rs1011970, which lies 246 kb centromeric within ANRIL, overlapping CDKN2B. Common variants at the 9p21 locus had not previously been associated with melanoma.
quotes: The third locus replicated is on 9p21, with the overall p-value reaching 4.03×l0−7 for rs7023329 which lies within the MTAP gene
plus another one, rsl011970, that is 246kb centromeric and is within ANRIL, an antisense non-coding mRNA starting in the promoter of p14/ARF gene and overlapping CDKN2B
Common variants within the 9p21 locus have not previously been associated with melanoma.

notes.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) found that rs1393350 at the TYR locus on chromosome 11 was associated with melanoma (P = 2.41 x 10(-14)). The TYR coding variant rs1126809 was also associated (OR 1.27). After accounting for rs1393350, no other SNP in the region was independently associated.
quotes: The chromosome 11 region (overall strongest evidence for rsl393350, p = 2.41×10−14) includes the TYR gene, which has previously been associated with melanoma; the coding variant (rsll26809) is included in the replication panel and shows a strong association in terms of OR for genotyped SNPs (OR = 1.27, 95% CI (1.16, 1.40), p = 1.17×10−6

notes.statement: Bishop et al. (2009) also confirmed melanoma association for the chromosome 20 region containing ASIP and for a chromosome 22 nevus-count locus (rs2284063). The effects at the three main loci did not interact and fit a multiplicative model. Effect sizes were notably homogeneous across European-ancestry populations living at different latitudes.
quotes: No pairwise interactions between the most significant SNPs at the three loci were significant (all p>0.19), showing that the pattern of association with the three loci is consistent with a multiplicative model

Despite wide variation in allele frequency, these genetic variants show notable homogeneity of effect across populations of European ancestry living at different latitudes and show independent association to disease risk.
this chromosomal region is confirmed by the present data

notes.statement: Herrero Hernández (2009) proposed pigmentation as a clue to understanding the link between Parkinson disease and melanoma.
quotes: Pigmentation as a clue to understanding Parkinson's disease and melanoma.

notes.statement: Passeron et al. (2009) found that SOX9 was expressed in normal human skin. It was increasingly downregulated as melanocytes progressed to premalignant, malignant, and metastatic states. In human and mouse melanoma cell lines, overexpressing SOX9 caused cell cycle arrest by increasing p21 transcription. It also restored sensitivity to retinoic acid by downregulating PRAME, and it inhibited tumorigenicity in mice and in a human ex vivo melanoma model.
quotes: Although SOX9 was expressed in normal human skin, it was increasingly downregulated as melanocytes progressed to the premalignant and then the malignant and metastatic states.

Overexpression of SOX9 in both human and mouse melanoma cell lines induced cell cycle arrest by increasing p21 transcription and restored sensitivity to RA by downregulating expression of PRAME, a melanoma antigen.
SOX9 overexpression in melanoma cell lines inhibited tumorigenicity both in mice and in a human ex vivo model of melanoma.

notes.statement: Passeron et al. (2009) found that treating melanoma cell lines with PGD2 increased SOX9 expression and restored retinoic acid sensitivity. Combined PGD2 and retinoic acid treatment substantially decreased tumor growth in human ex vivo and mouse in vivo melanoma models. The authors suggested this pointed to a possible noncytotoxic approach to melanoma treatment.
quotes: Treatment of melanoma cell lines with PGD2 increased SOX9 expression and restored sensitivity to RA. Thus, combined treatment with PGD2 and RA substantially decreased tumor growth in human ex vivo and mouse in vivo models of melanoma.
suggest the encouraging possibility of a noncytotoxic approach to the treatment of melanoma

notes.statement: In 2 prospective US cohorts (38,641 men and 93,661 women), Gao et al. (2009) found that Parkinson disease (PD) risk rose as hair color got lighter. Compared with black hair, the pooled adjusted relative risks for PD were 1.40, 1.61 and 1.93 for brown, blond and red hair. The associations were strongest for PD with onset before age 70 years.
quotes: Pooled RRs for PD were 1 (reference), 1.40, 1.61, and 1.93 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.4) for black, brown, blond, and red hair, respectively, after adjusting for age, smoking, ethnicity, and other covariates.
The associations between hair color and PD were particularly strong for relative younger onset of PD (<70 yr) (adjusted RR for red vs black hair = 3.83; 95% confidence interval, 1.7-8.7).

notes.statement: In a nested case-control study (272 PD cases and 1,185 controls genotyped), Gao et al. (2009) found that homozygosity for the melanoma-associated MC1R Arg151Cys variant was associated with red hair. Cys/Cys homozygotes also had a higher PD risk than Arg/Arg homozygotes (adjusted RR 3.15). The authors suggested that the higher-than-expected co-occurrence of melanoma and PD may be explained at least in part by the association of both diseases with lighter hair color and the MC1R Arg151Cys variant, rather than by levodopa treatment.
quotes: The Cys/Cys genotype was associated with a higher PD risk, relative to the Arg/Arg genotype (adjusted RR=3.15; 95% CI: 1.06, 9.37) (Table 3).

Our findings suggest that the higher frequency of melanoma occurring among individuals with PD may be at least in part explained by the associations of both diseases with a lighter hair color and the MC1R Arg151Cys variant allele, rather than being an adverse effect of levodopa treatment as previously suggested.

notes.statement: In 2,443 melanoma cases and 30,839 controls from Iceland, Sweden, and Spain, Rafnar et al. (2009) found that the C allele of rs401681 was significantly associated with protection against cutaneous melanoma (OR = 0.88, P = 8.0 x 10(-4)). This SNP lies in an intron of CLPTM1L at the TERT-CLPTM1L locus on chromosome 5p15.33. The same allele was associated with increased risk of basal cell carcinoma and of lung, bladder, prostate, and cervical cancer.
quotes: Interestingly, we observed a significant association between rs401681(C) and protection against cutaneous melanoma (OR=0.88, P=8.0×10−4) in a sample set consisting of 2,443 melanoma cases and 30,839 controls from Iceland, Sweden and Spain.
rs2736098 corresponds to A305A in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) protein and rs401681 is in an intron of the CLPTM1L gene.

notes.statement: Rafnar et al. (2009) noted an earlier report on telomere length in people with skin cancer: short telomeres were associated with increased risk of basal cell carcinoma, whereas long telomeres were associated with increased risk of melanoma. In older never-smoking women, they found that rs401681(C) and rs2736098(A) were associated with shorter telomeres at nominal significance.
quotes: We note that a recently published study of telomere length in individuals with skin cancers showed that while short telomeres are associated with increased risk of BCC, long telomeres are associated with increased risk of melanoma.
In these subjects, rs401681(C) and rs2736098(A) were associated with shorter telomeres with nominal significance (P=0.017 and 0.027, respectively)

notes.statement: Rafnar et al. (2009) found no association between rs401681(C) and pigment phenotypes, including hair and eye colour, freckling, and Fitzpatrick skin-type score.
quotes: We found no association between rs401681(C) and either smoking status or nicotine addiction or any of several pigment phenotypes assessed (hair and eye colour, freckling or Fitzpatrick skin-type score)

notes.statement: In a Spanish case-control study of 131 consecutive melanoma patients and 245 sex- and age-matched controls, Fernandez et al. (2008) genotyped 23 SNPs in 6 pigmentation genes. The variant allele of the SLC45A2 c.1122C>G (p.Phe374Leu; rs16891982) polymorphism was associated with protection from malignant melanoma (OR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.24-0.70; P = 0.008 after adjustment for multiple testing).
quotes: This Spanish case-control study included 131 consecutive melanoma patients and 245 control subjects frequency-matched for sex and age.

We found that the variant allele of c.1122C>G, p.Phe374Leu (NCBI dbSNP rs16891982) in SLC45A2 (membrane associated transporter previously known as MATP) was associated with protection from MM (OR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.24-0.70; P=0.008 after adjustment for multiple testing).

notes.statement: Fernandez et al. (2008) found that the protective SLC45A2 allele was also associated with dark hair, dark skin, dark eye color, the presence of solar lentigines and childhood sunburns, which they took as supporting the association. They proposed SLC45A2 as a melanoma susceptibility gene in a light-skinned population.
quotes: This association was validated by the consistent link observed with dark hair, dark skin, dark eye color, and the presence of solar lentigins and childhood sunburns.
This is the first time SLC45A2 has been described as a melanoma susceptibility gene in a light-skinned population.

notes.statement: In European populations comprising 2,121 individuals with cutaneous melanoma (CM), 2,163 with basal cell carcinoma (BCC), and over 40,000 controls, Gudbjartsson et al. (2008) found that a haplotype near ASIP conferred significant risk of CM (OR = 1.45, P = 1.2 x 10(-9)) and BCC (OR = 1.33, P = 1.2 x 10(-6)).
quotes: comprising 2,121 individuals with CM, 2,163 individuals with BCC and over 40,000 controls

A haplotype near ASIP, known to affect a similar spectrum of pigmentation traits as MC1R variants, conferred significant risk of CM (odds ratio (OR) = 1.45, P = 1.2 x 10(-9)) and BCC (OR = 1.33, P = 1.2 x 10(-6)).

notes.statement: Gudbjartsson et al. (2008) found that the TYR variant encoding the R402Q substitution conferred risk of CM (OR = 1.21, P = 2.8 x 10(-7)) and BCC (OR = 1.14, P = 6.1 x 10(-4)). An eye color variant in TYRP1 was associated with risk of CM (OR = 1.15, P = 4.6 x 10(-4)). The association of all 3 variants was robust to adjustment for the effect of pigmentation.
quotes: The variant in TYR encoding the R402Q amino acid substitution, previously shown to affect eye color and tanning response, conferred risk of CM (OR = 1.21, P = 2.8 x 10(-7)) and BCC (OR = 1.14, P = 6.1 x 10(-4)).
An eye color variant in TYRP1 was associated with risk of CM (OR = 1.15, P = 4.6 x 10(-4)).
The association of all three variants is robust with respect to adjustment for the effect of pigmentation.

notes.statement: Schatton et al. (2008) identified a subpopulation enriched for human malignant melanoma-initiating cells (MMIC) defined by expression of the chemoresistance mediator ABCB5. ABCB5+ tumor cells detected in melanoma patients had a primitive molecular phenotype and correlated with clinical melanoma progression. In serial human-to-mouse xenotransplantation, ABCB5+ cells had greater tumorigenic capacity than ABCB5- bulk populations and re-established tumor heterogeneity.
quotes: Here we identify a subpopulation enriched for human malignant-melanoma-initiating cells (MMIC) defined by expression of the chemoresistance mediator ABCB5
ABCB5+ tumour cells detected in human melanoma patients show a primitive molecular phenotype and correlate with clinical melanoma progression.
In serial human-to-mouse xenotransplantation experiments, ABCB5+ melanoma cells possess greater tumorigenic capacity than ABCB5- bulk populations and re-establish clinical tumour heterogeneity.

notes.statement: Schatton et al. (2008) used in vivo genetic lineage tracking to show that ABCB5+ melanoma cells could self-renew and differentiate, producing both ABCB5+ and ABCB5- progeny. ABCB5- populations gave rise, at lower rates, only to ABCB5- cells.
quotes: In vivo genetic lineage tracking demonstrates a specific capacity of ABCB5+ subpopulations for self-renewal and differentiation, because ABCB5+ cancer cells generate both ABCB5+ and ABCB5- progeny, whereas ABCB5- tumour populations give rise, at lower rates, exclusively to ABCB5- cells.

notes.statement: In an initial proof-of-principle analysis, Schatton et al. (2008) found that systemic administration of a monoclonal antibody against ABCB5 inhibited tumor growth. The antibody was capable of inducing antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity in ABCB5+ MMIC. This suggested that targeting this tumorigenic minority population could be a therapeutic strategy.
quotes: systemic administration of a monoclonal antibody directed at ABCB5, shown to be capable of inducing antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity in ABCB5+ MMIC, exerted tumour-inhibitory effects.

notes.statement: Bale and Chakravarti (1987) presented evidence for autosomal dominant inheritance and pleiotropy of the cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM)/dysplastic nevus (DN) gene.
quotes: Evidence for autosomal dominance and pleiotropy of the cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM)/Dysplastic nevus (DN) gene.

notes.statement: In a cross-sectional survey, Ferreira et al. (2007) found neoplastic or preneoplastic skin lesions in 35 of 150 patients with Parkinson disease (23.3%) and in 20 of 146 age-matched controls (13.7%). The difference lost statistical significance after adjustment for gender. Actinic keratosis was seen in 29 patients with Parkinson disease (19%), and basal cell carcinoma was diagnosed in 4 (3%). The authors called their results nonconclusive but in agreement with previous studies suggesting an increased risk of skin cancer in Parkinson disease. They recommended screening for actinic keratosis, given its associated melanoma risk, in future epidemiologic studies.
quotes: Thirty-five PD patients (23.3%) presented skin lesions that could be classified as neoplastic or preneoplastic vs. 20 subjects in the control group (13.7%) (OR 95%, CI 1.92 [1.05, 3.51]). However, this difference lost statistical significance when adjusted for gender
Twenty-nine PD patients (19%) presented actinic keratosis and basal cell carcinoma was diagnosed in 4 patients (3%).
The frequency of actinic keratosis in PD patients and the associated risk to develop melanoma recommends its screening in future epidemiological studies.

notes.statement: Constantinescu et al. (2007) identified 5 cases of malignant melanoma in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort of patients with early Parkinson disease, compared with 1.5 expected for a standard healthy population. The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% CI, 1.1-7.8), so melanoma incidence was higher than expected. They found no association between levodopa therapy and melanoma incidence.
quotes: We identified all known cases of malignant melanoma (N = 5) in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort and compared that to published expected values (N = 1.5) for a standard healthy population.
The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-7.8), indicating that incidence of malignant melanoma was higher than expected.
We found no association between levodopa therapy and the incidence of melanoma.

notes.statement: Using high-resolution array-based comparative genomic hybridization, Zhang et al. (2006) looked at 283 known human miRNA genes in 227 ovarian cancer, breast cancer, and melanoma specimens. They found that 85.9% of genomic loci containing miRNA genes showed DNA copy number alterations in melanoma. Copy number changes correlated with miRNA expression, and miRNA-associated genes such as Dicer1 and Argonaute2 also showed high-frequency copy number abnormalities.
quotes: A high proportion of genomic loci containing miRNA genes exhibited DNA copy number alterations in ovarian cancer (37.1%), breast cancer (72.8%), and melanoma (85.9%)
Importantly, we show that miRNA copy changes correlate with miRNA expression.
we identified high frequency copy number abnormalities of Dicer1, Argonaute2, and other miRNA-associated genes in breast and ovarian cancer as well as melanoma.

notes.statement: Curtin et al. (2005) compared genome-wide DNA copy-number changes and BRAF and NRAS mutation status in 126 melanomas from 4 groups with differing ultraviolet exposure: 30 from skin with chronic sun-induced damage, 40 from skin without such damage, 36 acral, and 20 mucosal. They found significant differences in regional copy-number changes and BRAF mutation frequencies among the groups, and copy-number changes classified samples into the 4 groups with 70% accuracy.
quotes: We compared genome-wide alterations in the number of copies of DNA and mutational status of BRAF and N-RAS in 126 melanomas from four groups in which the degree of exposure to ultraviolet light differs
Samples could be correctly classified into the four groups with 70 percent accuracy on the basis of the changes in the number of copies of genomic DNA.

notes.statement: Curtin et al. (2005) found that 81% of melanomas on skin without chronic sun-induced damage had mutations in BRAF or NRAS, whereas most melanomas in the other groups had mutations in neither gene. Melanomas with wild-type BRAF or NRAS frequently had increased copy number of CDK4 and CCND1, implicating these as independent oncogenes.
quotes: Eighty-one percent of melanomas on skin without chronic sun-induced damage had mutations in BRAF or N-RAS; the majority of melanomas in the other groups had mutations in neither gene.
Melanomas with wild-type BRAF or N-RAS frequently had increases in the number of copies of the genes for cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and cyclin D1 (CCND1)

notes.statement: Curtin et al. (2005) concluded that the genetic alterations seen in melanomas at different sites and with different sun exposure indicate distinct genetic pathways in melanoma development.
quotes: The genetic alterations identified in melanomas at different sites and with different levels of sun exposure indicate that there are distinct genetic pathways in the development of melanoma

notes.statement: Alexander et al. (2004) studied 2 patients with melanoma-associated retinopathy (MAR) who had normal visual acuity but reduced contrast sensitivity. The loss was not specific to the magnocellular pathway. Instead, it depended on spatial frequency and was greatest at low to intermediate frequencies. The authors concluded that this pattern was consistent with the retinal bipolar cell dysfunction presumed to underlie MAR.
quotes: The contrast sensitivity deficits of patients with MAR under photopic conditions are not specific to the MC pathway, as proposed previously, but instead are related to the spatial frequency of the test target.

The overall pattern of contrast sensitivity loss shown by the patients with MAR is consistent with the dysfunction at the level of the retinal bipolar cells that is presumed to underlie the MAR syndrome.

notes.statement: TURKINGTON (1965) addressed a familial factor in malignant melanoma.
quotes: FAMILIAL FACTOR IN MALIGNANT MELANOMA.

notes.statement: SCHOCH (1963) reported a pedigree study and cytogenetic study of familial malignant melanoma.
quotes: FAMILIAL MALIGNANT MELANOMA. A PEDIGREE AND CYTOGENETIC STUDY.

notes.statement: SALAMON et al. (1963) wrote about whether malignant melanoma is hereditary. The text available does not say what they found.
quotes: A contribution to the question of heredity of malignant melanomas.

notes.statement: Gillanders et al. (2003) performed a genomewide linkage scan in 49 Australian pedigrees, each with at least 3 cases of cutaneous malignant melanoma and no CDKN2A or CDK4 involvement. In 9 families selected for early age at onset, the highest parametric lod score was 4.95 (theta = 0) at D1S2776 on 1p22, with a nonparametric lod score of 5.37.
quotes: A parametric LOD score of 4.65 (theta=0) and a nonparametric LOD score of 4.19 were found at D1S2779 in nine families selected for early age at onset.
with the highest parametric LOD score, 4.95 (theta=0) (nonparametric LOD score 5.37), at D1S2776

notes.statement: In 33 additional multiplex melanoma families, Gillanders et al. (2003) found further evidence of linkage to 1p22. In a nonparametric ordered sequential analysis based on age at diagnosis, the maximum lod score was 6.43 at D1S2779, reached when the 15 families with the earliest onset were included.
quotes: The highest LOD score, 6.43, was obtained at D1S2779 and occurred when the 15 families with the earliest ages at onset were included.

notes.statement: Gillanders et al. (2003) noted that mutations in CDKN2A and CDK4 account for only 20 to 25% of families with multiple cases of melanoma. They concluded that their data provided significant evidence for a novel melanoma susceptibility gene in chromosome band 1p22.
quotes: they account for only 20%-25% of families with multiple cases of CMM
These data provide significant evidence of a novel susceptibility gene for CMM located within chromosome band 1p22.

notes.statement: Fung et al. (2003) described eMelanoBase, an online database of germline variants observed in all loci implicated in familial melanoma susceptibility, established by the Melanoma Genetics Consortium. It was designed to take into account the consequences of CDKN2A variants for both p16INK4A and p14ARF, including exon 2 mutations that can impair both polypeptides and insertions/deletions that could theoretically generate p16INK4A-p14ARF fusion proteins.
quotes: As an initiative of the international Melanoma Genetics Consortium, we have therefore established a database of germline variants observed in all loci implicated in familial melanoma susceptibility.
Mutations in exon 2 can impair both polypeptides and insertions and deletions in exons 1alpha, 1beta, and 2, which can theoretically generate p16INK4A-p14ARF fusion proteins.

notes.statement: Pollock et al. (2003) analysed microdissected melanoma and nevus samples. They found BRAF mutations resulting in the V599E substitution in 41 of 60 (68%) melanoma metastases, 4 of 5 (80%) primary melanomas, and, unexpectedly, 63 of 77 (82%) nevi.
quotes: We observed mutations resulting in the V599E amino-acid substitution in 41 of 60 (68%) melanoma metastases, 4 of 5 (80%) primary melanomas and, unexpectedly, in 63 of 77 (82%) nevi.

notes.statement: Pollock et al. (2003) concluded that mutational activation of the RAS/RAF/MAPK pathway in nevi is a critical step in the initiation of melanocytic neoplasia but alone is insufficient for melanoma tumorigenesis.
quotes: These data suggest that mutational activation of the RAS/RAF/MAPK pathway in nevi is a critical step in the initiation of melanocytic neoplasia but alone is insufficient for melanoma tumorigenesis.

notes.statement: Tucker et al. (2002) followed 33 melanoma-prone families, each with more than 2 living members with invasive melanoma, for up to 25 years. They examined and photographed 844 family members and found that most dysplastic nevi stayed stable or regressed, and few changed in a way that should raise concern for melanoma. They concluded that melanomas can be found early with careful surveillance.
quotes: Thirty-three families with > 2 living members with invasive melanoma were evaluated clinically and followed prospectively for up to 25 years.
The majority of dysplastic nevi either remain stable or regress; few change in a manner that should cause concern for melanoma. With careful surveillance, melanomas can be found early.

notes.statement: Tucker et al. (2002) found that the melanomas and dysplastic nevi in their study families did not appear to differ by the type of mutation in the family: CDKN2A, CDK4, or no identified mutation.
quotes: The melanomas and dysplastic nevi that were found to occur in the study families did not appear to vary by the type of mutation identified in the families.

notes.statement: Potter et al. (2002) described a woman with metastatic melanoma and melanoma-associated retinopathy whose serum contained antibodies to retinal transducin, but no immunoreactivity to retinal bipolar cells. They concluded that melanoma-associated retinopathy can be related to a variety of antiretinal antibodies and that transducin is a novel melanoma-associated retinopathy antigen.
quotes: Antibodies to a retinal transducin were demonstrated by Western blotting. No immunoreactivity to retinal bipolar cells was detected by immunohistochemistry.

Melanoma-associated retinopathy can be related to a variety of antiretinal antibodies. Recognition of transducin, a novel melanoma-associated retinopathy antigen, may be important for identifying and treating patients with night blindness and melanoma.

notes.statement: Davies et al. (2002) found somatic missense mutations in the BRAF gene in 66% of malignant melanomas, and at lower frequency in a wide range of other human cancers. All of the mutations were within the kinase domain, and a single substitution, V599E, accounted for 80% of them.
quotes: Here we report BRAF somatic missense mutations in 66% of malignant melanomas and at lower frequency in a wide range of human cancers.
All mutations are within the kinase domain, with a single substitution (V599E) accounting for 80%.

notes.statement: Davies et al. (2002) showed that mutated BRAF proteins had elevated kinase activity and transformed NIH3T3 cells. RAS function was not required for the growth of cancer cell lines carrying the V599E mutation.
quotes: Mutated BRAF proteins have elevated kinase activity and are transforming in NIH3T3 cells. Furthermore, RAS function is not required for the growth of cancer cell lines with the V599E mutation.

notes.statement: Davies et al. (2002) suggested that, because BRAF is a serine/threonine kinase commonly activated by somatic point mutation in human cancer, it may provide new therapeutic opportunities in malignant melanoma.
quotes: As BRAF is a serine/threonine kinase that is commonly activated by somatic point mutation in human cancer, it may provide new therapeutic opportunities in malignant melanoma.

notes.statement: Using a genetically engineered mouse model, Noonan et al. (2001) showed that a single dose of burning ultraviolet radiation given to neonates, but not to adults, was necessary and sufficient to induce tumors with high penetrance that resembled human melanoma. The authors concluded that this supported epidemiologic evidence that childhood sunburn poses a significant risk of developing melanoma.
quotes: Here we use a genetically engineered mouse model to show that a single dose of burning ultraviolet radiation to neonates, but not adults, is necessary and sufficient to induce tumours with high penetrance which are reminiscent of human melanoma.
Our results provide experimental support for epidemiological evidence that childhood sunburn poses a significant risk of developing this potentially fatal disease.

notes.statement: Hejny et al. (2001) reported 7 patients who developed retinopathy during high-dose interferon alfa-2b adjuvant therapy for high-risk melanoma. Five had normal visual acuity, with cotton-wool spots and/or retinal hemorrhages that resolved after treatment was stopped. Two developed severe retinopathy with vision loss to counting fingers or hand motions that did not resolve. Retinopathy was detected after 6 to 26 weeks of maintenance treatment, at total doses of 816 to 1770 million units.
quotes: Five patients had normal visual acuity, but retinopathy with cotton- wool spots and/or retinal hemorrhages with the retinopathy resolved after stopping treatment after detection. Two patients developed severe retinopathy with vision loss to counting fingers and hand motions without resolution of the retinopathy.

The duration of the maintenance treatment before detection of the retinopathy for all patients ranged from 6 to 26 weeks. The total dose received at time of detection of retinopathy ranged from 816 to 1770 million units.

notes.statement: Hejny et al. (2001) concluded that patients receiving interferon alfa-2b are at risk for an associated retinopathy and that the risk appears to be greater at higher doses. They recommended monitoring patients until the retinopathy resolves to screen for sequelae such as retinal neovascularization. They noted that it is unknown whether selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors such as paroxetine increase the incidence of this complication.
quotes: Patients receiving interferon alfa-2b are at risk for developing an associated retinopathy. The risk appears to be greater with higher dosage therapy.
Patients need to be monitored until the retinopathy is resolved to screen for sequelae, including retinal neovascularization.

notes.statement: Gilchrest et al. (1999) reviewed the pathogenesis of melanoma induced by ultraviolet radiation.
quotes: The pathogenesis of melanoma induced by ultraviolet radiation.

notes.statement: Goldstein et al. (1996) did two-trait-locus, two-marker-locus linkage analysis in 19 cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevi (CMM/DN) kindreds. Earlier analyses of these kindreds had shown linkage and heterogeneity to both 1p and 9p. For CMM alone, the single-locus heterogeneity model gave the highest LOD score (Z = 8.48 at theta = 0.0). The evidence for linkage to 9p was much stronger than for 1p, with LOD scores about 2 times greater.
quotes: Previous linkage analyses of 19 cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevi (CMM/DN) kindreds showed significant evidence of linkage and heterogeneity to both chromosomes 1p and 9p.

The LOD scores for CMM alone were highest using the SL-Het model (Z = 8.48, theta = .0). There was much stronger evidence of linkage to chromosome 9p than to 1p for CMM alone; the LOD scores were approximately two times greater on 9p than on 1p.

notes.statement: Goldstein et al. (1996) found that a chromosome 1p locus (or loci) appeared to contribute to both CMM and CMM/DN, whereas a 9p locus contributed more to CMM alone. Under 2-locus models, 1p LOD scores were higher for CMM/DN than for CMM alone, while 9p LOD scores were substantially lower. After conditioning on linkage to the other locus, only the 9p locus consistently showed significant evidence of linkage to CMM alone.
quotes: The change in LOD scores from an evaluation of CMM alone to CMM/DN suggested that a chromosome 1p locus (or loci) contributed to both CMM and CMM/DN, whereas a 9p locus contributed more to CMM alone.
In contrast, for 9p, the LOD scores were substantially lower with CMM/DN than with CMM alone (Ep: 4.64 vs. 7.06; Het: 5.38 vs. 7.99, respectively).
After conditioning on linkage to the other locus, only the 9p locus consistently showed significant evidence for linkage to CMM alone.

notes.statement: In 13 melanoma families, Goldstein et al. (1993) found a maximum lod score of 3.12 at theta = 0.10 between cutaneous malignant melanoma alone and the chromosome 1p marker D1S47, and a maximum lod of 1.76 at theta = 0.10 with D1S160; PND showed no evidence for linkage to CMM alone.
quotes: For CMM alone and D1S47, Zmax = 3.12 at theta = .10. For D1S160 and CMM alone, Zmax = 1.76 at theta = .10. PND showed no evidence for linkage to CMM alone.

notes.statement: Goldstein et al. (1993) found significant evidence for heterogeneity of CMM/DN linkage to 1p markers when families were split by proportion of CMM/DN cases (D1S47 and D1S160) or by occurrence of immune-related tumors (D1S160), with only a subset of families appearing linked to 1p. They concluded that diagnostic, clinical, and genetic heterogeneity are the likely reasons previous studies failed to confirm linkage.
quotes: In group 1 there was significant evidence of heterogeneity with both D1S47 and D1S160, and in group 2 there was significant evidence of heterogeneity with D1S160.
Thus, diagnostic, clinical, and genetic heterogeneity are the likely reasons that previous studies have failed to confirm linkage of CMM/DN to chromosome 1p.
significant evidence for heterogeneity with only a subset of the families appearing linked to chromosome 1p

notes.statement: Elder et al. (1980) reviewed clinical photographs of 79 prospectively studied cases of non-familial cutaneous malignant melanoma and proposed that patients with dysplastic nevi represent a distinctive syndrome, the dysplastic nevus syndrome, at increased risk for primary cutaneous melanoma. The dysplastic nevi were identical to the melanoma precursor lesion previously described in the familial B-K mole syndrome; this was the first description of such dysplasia in non-familial melanoma.
quotes: Clinical photographs of 79 prospectively studied cases of non-familial cutaneous malignant melanoma were reviewed
It is suggested that these patients represent a distinctive syndrome, the Dysplastic Nevus Syndrome (DNS) and that they are at increased risk for development of primary cutaneous malignant melanoma.

The clinically and histologically distinctive dysplastic nevi of these patients are identical to the precursor lesion for melanoma that we have previously described in a familial context, the B-K mole syndrome.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1980) observed vertical transmission, including father-to-son, of cutaneous malignant melanoma and/or FAMMM moles with no sex predilection in 3 kindreds. Together with other reports, they considered this consistent with an autosomal dominant gene showing markedly variable expressivity.
quotes: Findings showed vertical transmission, including father-to-son, of cutaneous malignant melanoma and/or FAMMM moles with no sex predilection.
These observations, when coupled with recent reports by others, are consistent with an autosomal dominant gene showing markedly variable expressivity.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1980) described a broad range of expression of the FAMMM phenotype, from apparent lack of disease expression through minimal, moderate, and florid manifestations. The degree of dysplasia in moles varied markedly between and within families.
quotes: A broad spectrum of clinical signs characterizing the phenotype ranged from an apparent lack of disease expression through minimal, moderate, and florid manifestations.
Of further interest was marked variation in the degree of dysplasia in moles between and within families.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1980) noted that management of FAMMM patients is difficult because it cannot be known for certain which moles need biopsy or which will need wider excision after histologic study. They stressed the lifelong susceptibility to multiple melanomas and the possibility that cancers at other sites may be part of the syndrome.
quotes: Management of these patients is difficult, as one cannot be certain which moles require biopsy and then, following histological study, which will require wider excision.
including the patient's lifelong susceptibility to multiply malignant melanomas, and the possibility that cancer of other anatomic sites may be integral components of this hereditary cancer syndrome.

notes.statement: Elder et al. (1982) proposed their definition of the dysplastic nevus syndrome.
quotes: The dysplastic nevus syndrome: our definition.

notes.statement: Happle et al. (1982) argued that precursor nevi are inherited polygenically.
quotes: Arguments in favor of a polygenic inheritance of precursor nevi.

notes.statement: Pellegris et al. (1982) typed HLA-A, -B, and -C in 6 families with familial malignant melanoma and found the HLA-B12 antigen in 5 of them. Linkage between HLA and familial melanoma could be analyzed in 3 families. Linkage was possible in 2 of these families but not in the third.
quotes: The HLA-B12 antigen was present in five of the six families.
In three families the HLA-FMM linkage could be analyzed: linkage was possible in two but not in the third.

notes.statement: Pellegris et al. (1982) suggested that there may be two types of familial melanoma: a more frequent type that apparently segregates with the HLA complex and another that does not. They proposed that two complementary factors, one of them in the HLA complex, promote familial melanoma with dominant inheritance and high penetrance.
quotes: These findings suggested that two types of FMM may exist: a more frequent type (five cases) that apparently segregates with the HLA complex and another (one case) that does not segregate with the HLA complex.
These findings are consistent with the hypothesis of two complementary factors (one of which was included in the HLA complex) for the promotion of FMM with dominant inheritance and high penetrance.

notes.statement: Hawkins et al. (1981) reported evidence for linkage between HLA and malignant melanoma.
quotes: Evidence for linkage between HLA and malignant melanoma.

notes.statement: Becher et al. (1983) analyzed G-banded chromosomes in short-term cultures of 4 malignant melanomas. They found 27 abnormal chromosomes, mostly translocations, followed by deletions and isochromosomes. All 4 cases had markers derived from chromosomes 1 and 6, and 3 had abnormalities of chromosome 7. No marker was shared between cases. The authors suggested that abnormalities of chromosomes 6 and 7 may be characteristic of malignant melanoma. They thought chromosome 1 aberrations may reflect a general feature of human neoplasia.
quotes: Chromosomes 1, 6, and 7 were found to be most frequently involved in structural aberrations. Markers originating from chromosomes 1 and 6 were found in all four cases, and abnormalities of chromosome 7 were found in three.

we suggest that abnormalities involving chromosomes 6 and 7 may be a characteristic feature of MM. Aberrations of chromosome 1, although common in MM, may be part of a general cytogenetic feature in human neoplasia.
