notes.statement: Trent et al. (1983) performed chromosome banding analysis on 5 cases of human malignant melanoma and found deletion or translocation of chromosome 6q in 4 of them. They compared their results with earlier published studies and suggested that 6q may be a specific site of chromosome aberration in malignant melanoma.
quotes: Results demonstrated a variety of chromosome alterations, including deletion or translocation of chromosome 6q, in four of five cases.
chromosome 6q may represent a specific site of chromosome aberration in malignant melanoma

notes.statement: Becher et al. (1983) found frequent involvement of chromosome 6 in structural aberrations on cytogenetic analysis of malignant melanoma cells from a number of cases.
quotes: Cytogenetic analysis of malignant melanoma (MM) cells from a number of cases revealed the frequent involvement of chromosome 6 in structural aberrations.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1983) described the familial atypical multiple mole-melanoma syndrome (FAMMM) as an autosomal dominantly inherited susceptibility to multiple atypical moles. The moles were coloured black, brown, tan, red, or pink and were sometimes variegated. They were 1 cm or larger, macular or papular, had regular or irregular borders, and were found mostly on areas not exposed to the sun. A patient could have few or none, or more than 100.
quotes: The familial atypical multiple mole-melanoma syndrome (FAMMM) is characterised by an autosomal dominantly inherited susceptibility to multiple atypical moles which show variable colouration ranging from black to brown, tan, red, or pink, with occasional variegation.
They may be few in number or absent or may exceed 100 in a given patient. They are located predominantly on areas not exposed to the sun.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1983) reported that the histopathology of FAMMM naevi showed dysplastic melanocytes, fibroplasia, a focal chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate, and new blood vessel formation in the papillary dermis. These findings were not present in every case.
quotes: Dysplastic changes in melanocytes, fibroplasia, focal chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate, and new blood vessel formation of the papillary dermis characterise their histopathology. These findings are not uniformly present.

notes.statement: In a single FAMMM kindred, Lynch et al. (1983) observed that some members had minimal or no skin signs, while others had a wider range of neoplasms. The authors attributed both findings to pleiotropic effects of the cancer-prone FAMMM genotype.
quotes: These latter phenomena, which we ascribe to the pleiotropic effects of the cancer-prone FAMMM genotype, were observed in a single FAMMM kindred, the subject of this report.

notes.statement: Arndt (1984) discussed congenital nevi and dysplastic nevi as precursors to malignant melanoma.
quotes: Precursors to malignant melanoma: congenital and dysplastic nevi.

notes.statement: Ochi et al. (1984) karyotyped a recurrent metastatic malignant melanoma on 3 separate occasions. They found 2 different clones, one hypodiploid and one hypertriploid, which shared the same marker chromosomes, der(6)t(6;17) and der(17)t(1;17). The authors suggested that the 2 clones reflected differences in morphology and the results of therapy.
quotes: We found two different clones, one hypodiploid and another hypertriploid; however, both clones had the same markers [i.e., der(6),t(6;17), and der(17),t(1;17)].
Detailed analysis of the histopathology and clinical course suggests that these two different clones reflected different morphology and results of therapy.

notes.statement: Pathak et al. (1983) analyzed G-banded karyotypes of 9 established human malignant melanoma cell lines and found that chromosome 6 was involved in marker chromosomes in all of them. In a review of their cases and the literature, 38 of 47 (80.8%) karyotyped melanoma cell lines or primary melanoma cells had a marker involving chromosome 6.
quotes: Analysis of G-banded chromosomes identified a number of altered (marker) chromosomes in these cell lines; in all the lines, chromosome 6 was found to be involved in the marker chromosomes.
A review of the literature and these cases showed that of 47 cell lines or primary melanoma cells karyotyped, 38 (80.8%) had a marker involving the 6.

notes.statement: Pathak et al. (1983) proposed that a genetic factor determining melanoma initiation is located in the distal segment of 6q. They suggested that deletion of this segment or of the entire 6q makes the melanoblast or melanocyte malignant.
quotes: We believe that the genetic factor determining melanoma initiation is located in the distal segment of 6q. Deletion of this segment or the entire 6q is responsible for the cell's (melanoblast or melanocyte) becoming malignant.

notes.statement: Balaban et al. (1984) studied the chromosomes of melanocytic lesions from 17 patients. The 5 nevi, 3 of them dysplastic, had normal karyotypes, but each tumor had a mostly abnormal karyotype. In 10 of the 11 advanced melanomas, chromosome 1 was involved; in 9 of these, deletions or translocations of 1p involved the proximal segment 1p12-p22.
quotes: The 5 nevi had normal karyotypes, while each of the tumors had a predominantly abnormal karyotype.

Ten of the 11 advanced melanomas had one or more aberrations involving chromosome #1, with 9 having deletions or translocations of lp that involved the proximal segment 1p12----1p22 9 times in 8 lesions.

notes.statement: Balaban et al. (1984) found extra 7q material in 6 advanced melanomas: 4 had extra copies of chromosome 7 and 2 had 7q+. Nine melanomas, including an early pseudodiploid tumor with a 6p;22 translocation, had changes in chromosome 6, and 3 of these had extra copies of 6p. The authors suggested that genes important in melanoma development lie on proximal 1p, on 7q and on chromosome 6.
quotes: Six advanced tumors had additional material involving 7q, including extra #7s (4 cases) and 7q+ (2 cases). Nine melanomas, including the early tumor, had alterations in chromosome #6.
The nonrandom cytogenetic changes suggest that genes important in melanoma carcinogenesis are located on the proximal portion of 1p, on 7q, and on chromosome #6.

notes.statement: In one advanced tumor, Balaban et al. (1984) found that the primary lesion and 5 metastases removed one after another over 18 months had nearly identical karyotypes. They took this as evidence that the tumor was clonal.
quotes: In one advanced tumor, the primary lesion and 5 metastases (removed seriatim over an 18-month period) had nearly identical karyotypes, indicating the clonal nature of the neoplasm.

notes.statement: Greene et al. (1983) did segregation analysis on 401 members of 14 high-risk kindreds with familial cutaneous malignant melanoma (CMM) and dysplastic nevus syndrome (DNS). The findings fit autosomal dominant inheritance of the familial CMM trait. A similar model probably applied to DNS, but segregation analysis could not confirm a major locus.
quotes: Pedigree analysis was compatible with an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance for the familial CMM trait.
Although a similar model probably applies to the DNS trait as well, segregation analysis could not confirm the presence of a major locus.

notes.statement: Greene et al. (1983) ran linkage analysis with 23 genetic markers in 14 melanoma-prone kindreds. Their results suggested that a DNS/CMM susceptibility gene may lie on the short arm of chromosome 1, within 30 map units of the Rh locus (maximum lod score = 2.00).
quotes: linkage analysis suggested that an autosomal dominant model was appropriate for the DNS, and that a DNS/CMM susceptibility gene may be located on the short arm of chromosome 1, within 30 map units of the Rh locus [maximum logarithm of odds (lod) score = 2.00].

notes.statement: Howell et al. (1984) found that skin fibroblast strains from 5 patients with hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma and the dysplastic nevus syndrome were all more sensitive than normal to killing by 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide (4NQO), with 2- to 3-fold steeper survival curves, whereas only 1 strain was hypersensitive to killing by simulated sunlight.
quotes: All five strains tested were more sensitive than normal to the killing effect of 4NQO (slopes of survival curves were 2- to 3-fold steeper), but only one strain was hypersensitive to killing by Sun Lamp radiation.

notes.statement: Howell et al. (1984) found that 2 strains tested for mutagenicity (6-thioguanine resistance) were both hypermutable after 4NQO exposure, and 1 showed an increased frequency of mutants induced by simulated sunlight. They suggested that hypersensitivity to mutagens contributes to melanoma risk in these patients and supports the somatic cell mutation hypothesis of cancer.
quotes: Both strains were hypermutable after exposure to 4NQO, but only one showed a higher than normal frequency of mutants induced by simulated sunlight.
suggests that hypersensitivity to mutagens contributes to risk of melanoma in patients. It also supports the somatic cell mutation hypothesis for the origin of cancer.

notes.statement: Kraemer et al. (1983) wrote about dysplastic naevi in relation to the risk of cutaneous melanoma.
quotes: Dysplastic naevi and cutaneous melanoma risk.

notes.statement: Greene et al. (1980) proposed a nomenclature for the precursor naevi of cutaneous malignant melanoma.
quotes: Precursor naevi in cutaneous malignant melanoma: a proposed nomenclature.

notes.statement: Lynch and Krush (1968) discussed heredity in malignant melanoma and what it means for early cancer detection.
quotes: Heredity and malignant melanoma: implications for early cancer detection.

notes.statement: Anderson (1971) described the clinical characteristics of the genetic variety of cutaneous melanoma in man.
quotes: Clinical characteristics of the genetic variety of cutaneous melanoma in man.

notes.statement: Rhodes et al. (1985) found that 8 of 65 sibs (12.3%) of 39 probands with small congenital nevomelanocytic nevi also had such nevi. This was 11 times the population prevalence in newborns (1.1%). They also found an affected parent in 5 of the 39 families. They concluded that small congenital nevi may cluster in families, and that either autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance or multifactorial determination could explain this.
quotes: This prevalence rate in sibs is 11 times the population-based prevalence rate of CNN in newborn infants (1.1%)
We conclude that small CNN may aggregate in families. Autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance or multifactorial determination could account for this observation.

notes.statement: Bale et al. (1985) performed HLA typing in 11 families with hereditary cutaneous malignant melanoma and dysplastic nevi and reanalyzed published data from 19 other families. With CMM as the trait, linkage to HLA was rejected for all recombination fractions less than 40% in the pooled 30 families, and analysis of the combined CMM/dysplastic nevus trait in 18 families also gave strong evidence against linkage.
quotes: When data from all 30 families were pooled and CMM was defined as the disease trait, the hypothesis of linkage was rejected for all values of recombination (theta) less than 40%.
Linkage analysis between the combined CMM/DN trait and HLA provided strong evidence against this hypothesis.

notes.statement: Bale et al. (1985) observed significant heterogeneity among subgroups of families. They suggested that preferential reporting of positive linkage results and misclassification of subjects' susceptibility status may have contributed to the earlier belief that the hereditary melanoma gene was linked to HLA.
quotes: Significant heterogeneity was observed when various sub-groups of families were compared; these data suggested that preferential reporting of positive linkage findings and misclassification of study subjects' CMM susceptibility status may have contributed to previous beliefs that the hereditary melanoma gene was linked to HLA.

notes.statement: Greene et al. (1985) described the familial dysplastic nevus syndrome and identified dysplastic nevi as acquired precursors of cutaneous malignant melanoma.
quotes: Acquired precursors of cutaneous malignant melanoma. The familial dysplastic nevus syndrome.

notes.statement: Rey et al. (1985) used G-banding to study direct and in vitro preparations of a malignant melanoma that had spread to the brain. The tumor cells had a pseudodiploid modal chromosome number and 5 marker chromosomes, one of which was an i(6p). The authors said these results agreed with recent reports that chromosome 6 is preferentially involved in malignant melanoma.
quotes: showed a pseudodiploid modal chromosome number, including five marker chromosomes, one of which was an i(6p)
These results agree with those recently reported about the preferential involvement of chromosome #6 in malignant melanoma.

notes.statement: Kopf et al. (1986) used prospectively completed questionnaires on 1,169 patients with cutaneous malignant melanoma, of whom 69 reported a family history of melanoma. Compared with nonfamilial cases, familial melanoma was significantly associated with a younger age at first diagnosis, a smaller lesion diameter, a lower Clark level, and fewer nonmelanoma skin cancers and noncutaneous cancers. The authors suggested that greater awareness of melanoma among family members could account for some of these observations.
quotes: those that significantly correlated with the familial occurrence of malignant melanoma include younger age at first diagnosis, smaller diameter of the lesion, lower Clark level, decreased frequency of nonmelanoma skin cancer, and reduced prevalence of noncutaneous cancer.
Increased awareness of malignant melanoma among family members could account for some of these observations.

notes.statement: Kopf et al. (1986) concluded that recognizing familial malignant melanoma has practical implications for early detection and prompt intervention.
quotes: Identification of the familial variety of malignant melanoma has practical implications concerning early detection and prompt intervention.

notes.statement: Hartley et al. (1987) described 7 cases of malignant melanoma in close relatives of children with osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma. They proposed that in certain families, malignant melanoma may be another manifestation of the same gene defect that causes susceptibility to the tumors of the SBLA cancer family syndrome, including childhood adrenal cortical carcinoma, osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and retinoblastoma.
quotes: Seven cases of malignant melanoma in the close relatives of children with osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma are described.

it is proposed that in certain families malignant melanoma may be another manifestation of the same gene defect which results in susceptibility to tumours characteristic of the SBLA cancer family syndrome

notes.statement: Bale et al. (1986) used life-table and disease-free survival analysis and estimated that the lifetime incidence of melanoma in the sibs and offspring of individuals with dysplastic nevi was 46%. They considered this consistent with a highly penetrant, autosomal dominant mode of inheritance.
quotes: we estimated the lifetime incidence of melanoma in the sibs and offspring of DN-affected individuals to be 46%, consistent with a highly penetrant, autosomal dominant mode of inheritance

notes.statement: Bale et al. (1986) ran a linkage analysis between the melanoma locus and a hypothetical dysplastic nevus locus and obtained a maximum lod score of 3.857 at theta = 0.08. All families that gave evidence for linkage were in the coupling phase, and the maximum likelihood estimate of theta did not differ significantly from 0. The authors concluded that dysplastic nevi and melanoma may be pleiotropic effects of a single, highly penetrant autosomal dominant gene.
quotes: we conducted a linkage analysis between the melanoma locus and a hypothetical DN locus, and obtained a maximum lod score of 3.857 at theta = .08
all families giving evidence for linkage were in the coupling phase and the maximum likelihood estimate of theta was not significantly different from 0 (P = .1)
the DN and melanoma traits may represent pleiotropic effects of a single, highly penetrant gene behaving in an autosomal dominant manner

notes.statement: Traupe et al. (1989) estimated mutation rates for the dysplastic nevus 'syndrome.' Derived directly from sporadic occurrence, the rate was exceedingly high (0.9-2.5%), whereas by Haldane's formula it would be 0.007-0.02%, so that new mutations would outnumber eliminated ones by 100:1. They concluded that this apparent lack of genetic equilibrium is not compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance of the dysplastic nevus syndrome.
quotes: When derived directly from the sporadic occurrence of the trait, the mutation rate is exceedingly high (0.9%-2.5%), whereas, as estimated with the aid of Haldane's formula it would be 0.007% to 0.02%. Accordingly, newly arising mutation would outnumber eliminated mutations by 100:1.
The apparent lack of a genetic equilibrium between newly arising and eliminated mutations is not compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance of the dysplastic nevus "syndrome."

notes.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1987) studied cell lines from 6 independent metastases of one melanoma patient. They found loss of heterozygosity in the tumor cells on 8 of the 16 informative autosomes and at all 3 informative X-linked loci. With one exception, there were no karyotypic abnormalities in the regions that showed loss of heterozygosity.
quotes: Segregations resulting in the loss of heterozygosity were detected in the tumor cells at 8 of 16 autosomes with at least 1 informative locus and at the 3 informative X-linked loci.
With a single exception, karyotypic abnormalities were not detected in the region of loci where loss of heterozygosity had been detected.

notes.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1987) found that all 6 metastases had inactivated the same X chromosome and showed identical segregation at loci on chromosomes 9 and X, which supported a monoclonal origin. From the patterns of segregation they built a genealogy of tumor progression and proposed a model in which metastatic cells accumulate selectively neutral and advantageous segregations.
quotes: The monoclonal derivation of the 6 metastases is supported by the inactivation of the same X-chromosome and the presence of identical segregation at loci on chromosomes 9 and X.
the development of a model of tumor progression which describes the accumulation of selectively neutral and advantageous segregations in metastatic tumor cells

notes.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1989) tested 35 melanomas and 21 melanoma cell lines for loss of constitutional heterozygosity at loci on chromosome 1p. They found 1p loss of heterozygosity in 15 of 35 (43%) melanomas and in 11 of 21 (52%) cell lines.
quotes: Loss-of-heterozygosity at loci on chromosome 1p was identified in 15/35 (43%) melanomas and 11/21 (52%) melanoma cell lines.

notes.statement: Dracopoli et al. (1989) studied multiple metastases from the same patient, and melanoma and lymphoblastoid samples from a family with hereditary melanoma. They concluded that loss of heterozygosity on distal 1p is a late event in tumor progression. It is not the second mutation that a cellular recessive mechanism for melanoma would predict.
quotes: showed that the loss-of-heterozygosity at loci on distal 1p is a late event in tumor progression, rather than the second mutation that would occur if melanoma were due to a cellular recessive mechanism

notes.statement: Based on comparisons with neuroblastoma and multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2, Dracopoli et al. (1989) suggested that frequent 1p loss of heterozygosity in these cancers is a common late event in the progression of neuroectodermal tumors.
quotes: Comparisons with neuroblastoma and multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN2) suggest that the frequent 1p loss-of-heterozygosity in these malignancies is a common late event of neuroectodermal tumor progression.

notes.statement: Bale et al. (1989) studied six families with a predisposition to melanoma and, by multipoint linkage analysis with 26 polymorphic DNA markers on 1p, mapped a susceptibility gene for cutaneous malignant melanoma-dysplastic nevus to chromosome band 1p36, between D1S47 and the pronatrodilatin gene (PND). The odds were greater than 260,000:1 in favor of linkage at this location.
quotes: An analysis of the cosegregation of the cutaneous malignant melanoma-dysplastic nevus trait with 26 polymorphic DNA markers on the short arm of chromosome 1 demonstrated the presence of a gene for susceptibility to melanoma.

The gene was located between an anonymous DNA marker (D1S47) and the gene locus for pronatrodilatin, a commonly used reference gene (PND), in chromosome band 1p36. The odds were greater than 260,000:1 in favor of linkage at this location.

notes.statement: Vasen et al. (1989) compared melanomas in 9 Dutch families with dysplastic nevus syndrome. They grouped them as diagnosed before screening started, found at the first family examination, or found during follow-up. The average thickness of invasive melanomas was 1.75, 0.80 and 0.54 mm, respectively. Sixteen of 19 melanomas found before screening were Clark level III or IV, whereas 15 of 20 found during follow-up were Clark level I or II. The authors concluded that screening can detect melanomas at an earlier stage and can improve prognosis.
quotes: The average thickness of the invasive melanomas in categories I, II and III was 1.75, 0.80 and 0.54 mm respectively.
Sixteen of the 19 melanomas in category I (84%) were Clark III or IV, whereas 15 of the 20 melanomas in category III (75%) were Clark I or II.

From these findings it may be concluded that screening can lead to the detection of melanomas at an earlier stage, which in turn can permit curative treatment and improvement of both prognosis and life expectancy.

notes.statement: Hecht (1989) reviewed the description by Norris in 1820 of hereditary malignant melanoma of the skin.
quotes: The description by Norris of hereditary malignant melanoma of the skin in 1820.

notes.statement: Cannon-Albright et al. (1990) genotyped 3 Utah kindreds with multiple cases of melanoma for the markers PND and D1S47 on distal 1p. They found no evidence of linkage, whether they analyzed melanoma alone or a combined melanoma/dysplastic nevus phenotype. Multipoint linkage analysis excluded the CM/DNS locus from a 55-cM region that included the PND-D1S47 region.
quotes: Family members in these kindreds were genotyped for the two markers reported to be most closely linked in the Bale study, PND and D1S47.
By multipoint linkage analysis the CM/DNS locus was excluded from an area of 55 cM containing the PND-D1S47 region.

notes.statement: Cannon-Albright et al. (1990) suggested that diagnostic or genetic heterogeneity could explain why their results differed from the 1p36 linkage reported by Bale et al.
quotes: Diagnostic or genetic heterogeneity are alternate explanations for the discrepancy between our observations and those of Bale et al.

notes.statement: Millikin et al. (1991) used RFLP analysis of 20 matched melanoma tumor and normal DNA pairs and found loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 6q at 21 of 53 informative loci (40%). Five patients had allele losses consistent with loss of the entire long arm (or an entire copy) of chromosome 6, and 4 others had terminal deletions of 6q.
quotes: LOH on chromosome 6q was identified at 21 of 53 informative loci (40%).

Five patients with more than one informative locus had allele losses consistent with the loss of the entire long arm (or of an entire copy) of chromosome 6, while four other patients demonstrated terminal deletions of 6q.

notes.statement: Millikin et al. (1991) found the highest frequency of 6q allelic loss (60%) in the region defined by the c-MYB and ESR loci (6q22-q23 and 6q24-q27), whereas LOH at loci on chromosomes 1, 11, 16, and 17 occurred in only 5% of cases. They concluded that loss of 6q sequences is a nonrandom and possibly biologically relevant event in malignant melanoma.
quotes: The chromosomal region bearing the highest frequency of 6q allelic loss (60%) is defined by the marker loci c-MYB and ESR (6q22-23 and 6q24-27).
In contrast to the frequency of 6q loss, LOH was observed at loci on four other chromosomes (1, 11, 16, 17) in only 5% of cases.
the loss of sequences from the long arm of chromosome 6 is a nonrandom and possibly biologically relevant event in human malignant melanoma

notes.statement: In eight Australian families with hereditary melanoma, Kefford et al. (1991) studied eight polymorphic DNA markers on the short arm of chromosome 1, including D1S47 and PND. They found a strongly negative probability of linkage and effectively excluded the putative melanoma susceptibility gene from distal 1p in these families.
quotes: An analysis of the cosegregation of the cutaneous malignant melanoma/DN trait with eight polymorphic DNA markers on the short arm of chromosome 1, including the distally located DNA markers D1S47 and PND yielded a strongly negative probability of linkage.
The putative gene for susceptibility to melanoma in these families was effectively excluded from this region of the short arm of chromosome 1.

notes.statement: Kefford et al. (1991) found that their pedigrees fell into three groups: melanoma without dysplastic nevi, melanoma with occasional dysplastic nevi, and melanoma with dysplastic nevi. They suggested that hereditary melanoma is heterogeneous in its genetic basis and in its association with the dysplastic nevus syndrome.
quotes: Pedigrees fell into three groups: 1) hereditary melanoma alone with no associated DN, 2) hereditary melanoma with occasional DN-affected individuals, and 3) hereditary melanoma with DN.
These findings suggest that hereditary melanoma is heterogeneous in relation to the genetic basis and its association with the DNS.

notes.statement: In the eight families studied by Kefford et al. (1991), 15 family members had dysplastic nevi without melanoma.
quotes: An additional 15 family members had DN alone.

notes.statement: Nancarrow et al. (1992) ran linkage studies with 1p markers in 7 Australian familial melanoma kindreds, 3 of which were the largest reported worldwide. They excluded a melanoma gene from a 40-cM region spanning the D1S47-PND interval and extending about 15 cM beyond each marker. They also excluded about 20 cM around the MYCL1/D1S57 loci.
quotes: We have been able to exclude localization of an MLM gene from a 40-cM region that spans the interval between D1S47 and PND and extends approximately 15 cM on either side of these markers.
In addition, we can exclude a region of about 20 cM around the MYCL1/D1S57 loci.

notes.statement: Nancarrow et al. (1992) noted that whether a cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevus gene (CMM) maps to distal 1p, linked to PND and D1S47, was highly controversial. They also noted that no study had found support for linkage of familial melanoma alone to these markers.
quotes: Considerable controversy exists over the possible assignment of a cutaneous malignant melanoma/dysplastic nevus gene, designated CMM, to the distal short arm of chromosome 1, linked to the PND and D1S47 loci.
To date, no support for linkage of MLM alone to these markers has been found

notes.statement: Fountain et al. (1992) studied loss of heterozygosity at 8 markers on chromosome 9p in metastatic melanoma tumors and cell lines. Two or more loci were hemizygously reduced in 12 of 14 (86%) informative tumor and cell line DNAs. Homozygous deletions of marker D9S126 were seen in 2 of 20 (10%) melanoma cell lines.
quotes: Two or more of these loci were found to be hemizygously reduced in 12 of 14 (86%) informative metastatic melanoma tumor and cell line DNAs, and homozygous deletions of the marker D9S126 were observed in 2 of 20 (10%) melanoma cell lines.

notes.statement: Fountain et al. (1992) defined a small critical region of 2 to 3 Mb on 9p21 where a putative melanoma tumor-suppressor gene was likely to lie. They excluded IFNB1, the IFNA gene cluster, GGTB2 and the TYRP locus as candidates because these genes lay outside the homozygously deleted regions.
quotes: These findings have resulted in the identification of a small critical region of 2-3 megabases on 9p21 in which a putative melanoma tumor-suppressor gene appears likely to reside.

Several 9p candidate genes, including IFNB1, the IFNA gene cluster, GGTB2, and the tyrosinase-related protein (TYRP) locus, have all been eliminated as potential targets because they are located outside of the homozygously deleted regions.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1978) found that the cutaneous multiple-mole phenotype was transmitted in their family, and in several others then under investigation, in a pattern consistent with a simple autosomal dominant factor.
quotes: Transmission of the cutaneous phenotype in the subject family, and in several others currently under investigation, shows an inheritance pattern consistent with a simple autosomal dominant factor.

notes.statement: Lynch et al. (1978) proposed that this cutaneous phenotype indicated melanoma risk and could be added to the cancer-related genodermatoses.
quotes: This cutaneous phenotype signifying melanoma risk may now be added to an increasing body of knowledge dealing with cancer-related genodermatoses.

notes.statement: Clark et al. (1978) described distinctive melanocytic moles, designated the 'B-K mole syndrome,' in 37 members of 6 melanoma families: 15 of 17 examined melanoma patients and 22 of 41 nonmelanoma relatives had the moles. The moles numbered from fewer than 10 to more than 100, were prominent on the upper trunk and extremities, and varied in size (5 to 15 mm), outline, and color.
quotes: Among the family members examined by the authors, 15 of 17 patients with melanoma and 22 of 41 nonmelanoma relatives had the unique moles.

The clinical features of the syndrome include the presence of less than 10 to greater than 100 moles prominent of the upper trunk and extremities, and variability of mole size (5 mm to 15 mm), outline, and color combination.

notes.statement: Clark et al. (1978) found that B-K moles histologically showed atypical melanocytic hyperplasia, lymphocytic infiltration, delicate fibroplasia, and new blood vessels, arising within a compound nevus or de novo; transformation of 2 B-K moles into malignant melanoma was documented photographically.
quotes: Histologically, B-K moles show atypical melanocytic hyperplasia, lymphocytic infiltration, delicate fibroplasia, and new blood vessels that occur within a compound nevus or de novo.
The transformation of two B-K moles into malignant melanomas was documented photographically.

notes.statement: Greene et al. (1978) proposed that melanoma occurring in families may be related to an inherited syndrome of precursor skin lesions with distinct clinical and histologic features. They suggested that recognizing this syndrome in relatives of melanoma patients identifies family members at high risk for melanoma, which allows earlier diagnosis and treatment.
quotes: Familial occurrences of malignant melanoma may be related to an inherited syndrome of precursor cutaneous lesions with distinct clinical and histologic features.
Recognition of the syndrome in the relatives of melanoma patients identifies a subset of family members at high risk for melanoma, facilitating their early diagnosis and treatment.

notes.statement: Reimer et al. (1978) found pigmented lesions with distinctive clinical and histologic characteristics in 18 of 20 melanoma patients (90%) and in 24 of 43 first-degree relatives (56%) in 7 consecutive melanoma-prone families. Recognition of these lesions led to detection of early-stage melanoma in 6 family members.
quotes: In seven consecutive melanoma-prone families, pigmented lesions with distinctive clinical and histologic characteristics occurred in 18 of 20 melanoma patients (90%) and 24 of 43 first-degree relatives (56%).
Recognition of these lesions led to the detection of early-stage melanoma in six family members.

notes.statement: Reimer et al. (1978) concluded that this preneoplastic syndrome of distinctive pigmented lesions in melanoma-prone families appeared to represent an autosomal dominant trait.
quotes: This syndrome appears to represent an autosomal dominant trait and may serve as a cutaneous marker to identify persons at high risk for melanoma.

notes.statement: Reimer et al. (1978) suggested that the distinctive precursor pigmented lesions may serve as a cutaneous marker to identify persons at high risk for melanoma.
quotes: This syndrome appears to represent an autosomal dominant trait and may serve as a cutaneous marker to identify persons at high risk for melanoma.
